endCard.text: PART 2 — Follow so you don't miss it.
endCard.title: THE VILLAGE THAT REPEATS

narration.text: My name is Wren. Today is Tuesday. It has been Tuesday for four hundred and twelve days.

sentences.text: My name is Wren.
Today is Tuesday.
It has been Tuesday for four hundred and twelve days.

narration.text: Every morning, the bell rings at six. The baker drops his bread. The old man tells the same joke about the goat. And every morning, I'm the only one who remembers yesterday.

sentences.text: Every morning, the bell rings at six.
The baker drops his bread.
The old man tells the same joke about the goat.
And every morning, I'm the only one who remembers yesterday.

narration.text: I know this village better than anyone alive. I know which step creaks. I know the exact second the rain starts. I know that at seven fourteen, a stranger's cart rolls through the square, and never rolls out.

sentences.text: I know this village better than anyone alive.
I know which step creaks.
I know the exact second the rain starts.
I know that at seven fourteen, a stranger's cart rolls through the square, and never rolls out.

narration.text: I tried leaving. Every road bends back to the square. I tried staying awake all night. At dawn, I'm in my bed, and the bell is ringing.

sentences.text: I tried leaving.
Every road bends back to the square.
I tried staying awake all night.
At dawn, I'm in my bed, and the bell is ringing.

narration.text: I told my mother once. I told her everything. She smiled, patted my hair, and said, eat your breakfast, Wren. Tomorrow, she won't even remember I asked.

sentences.text: I told my mother once.
I told her everything.
She smiled, patted my hair, and said, eat your breakfast, Wren.
Tomorrow, she won't even remember I asked.

narration.text: But today is different. There's a chalk mark on my door. A tiny clock, stopped at three oh seven. I didn't draw it.

sentences.text: But today is different.
There's a chalk mark on my door.
A tiny clock, stopped at three oh seven.
I didn't draw it.

narration.text: More marks. On the well. The bakery wall. The mill. Each one pointing the same way, like breadcrumbs left by someone who wanted to be followed.

sentences.text: More marks.
On the well.
The bakery wall.
The mill.
Each one pointing the same way, like breadcrumbs left by someone who wanted to be followed.

narration.text: They led to the clock tower. The one place nobody is allowed to go. Even the old man stops his joke when he walks past it.

sentences.text: They led to the clock tower.
The one place nobody is allowed to go.
Even the old man stops his joke when he walks past it.

narration.text: The door was locked. But carved beneath the lock, in handwriting I'd know anywhere, because it's mine: don't trust the one who never forgets.

sentences.text: The door was locked.
But carved beneath the lock, in handwriting I'd know anywhere, because it's mine:
don't trust the one who never forgets.

narration.text: I've never been here before. Not once, in four hundred and twelve days. So when did I write it?

sentences.text: I've never been here before.
Not once, in four hundred and twelve days.
So when did I write it?

narration.text: Then the bell rang. Out of order. Nobody has ever heard it ring out of order. And someone behind me whispered my name... and they remembered it too.

sentences.text: Then the bell rang.
Out of order.
Nobody has ever heard it ring out of order.
And someone behind me whispered my name...
and they remembered it too.
